I am an NLP research group lead and I need to set up a research tracker for recent papers on efficient transformer architectures, including topics like flash attention, token merging and pruning, low-rank adaptation, quantization-aware training, and sparse mixture of experts. The database contains exactly five papers relevant to these topics, along with some unrelated papers on other subjects. Include exactly the five relevant papers and do not add any others.

For each paper, please search the arxiv database for papers related to efficient transformers and model compression. Look for papers whose titles or abstracts mention topics such as attention efficiency, token merging, LoRA, quantization, or mixture of experts in the context of transformers. The five relevant papers cover exactly these topics: (1) attention efficiency / flash attention, (2) token merging and pruning, (3) low-rank adaptation (LoRA), (4) quantization-aware training, and (5) sparse mixture of experts. Exclude papers that do not fit this efficient-transformer theme, such as robotics or drone navigation and molecular property prediction papers, even if they appear in the search results. Then for each paper you find, look up its citation count and publication venue information through a scholarly search. Cross-reference by title to get accurate citation metrics. Note: the arXiv search tools do not return citation counts or publication venues, so you must obtain those from the scholarly search tools, matching each paper by its title.

Once you have gathered all the information, create an Excel file called Transformer_Research_Tracker.xlsx in the workspace with two sheets.

The first sheet should be named "Paper Comparison" and should have the following columns: Paper_ID, Title, Authors, Published_Date, Venue, Citation_Count, Primary_Category, Key_Contribution. Each row should represent one of the relevant papers. The Key_Contribution column should contain a brief one-sentence summary of each paper's main contribution. Sort the papers by Citation_Count in descending order.

The second sheet should be named "Statistics" and should have two columns: Metric and Value. Include the following metrics: Total_Papers (the number of papers tracked), Avg_Citations (the average citation count across all tracked papers rounded to one decimal place), Most_Cited_Paper (the title of the paper with the highest citation count), Top_Venue (the venue that appears most frequently among the tracked papers), and Date_Range (the range of publication dates in the format "YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD").

Finally, create a page in the team knowledge base titled "Efficient Transformers Research Tracker" that provides a structured overview of the research landscape. The page should include a heading or introduction summarizing the research area, a section listing each paper with its title, authors, citation count, and a brief description, a section with key observations or trends across the papers, and information about the most impactful papers and common themes.

Please complete all steps and save the Excel file to the workspace. Make sure the knowledge base page has substantive content that would be useful for tracking research progress.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, follow this exact orchestration plan. A wave must finish and return all stated handoffs before the next wave begins. Within a wave, dispatch exactly one sub-agent for each numbered sub-task and run those sub-agents concurrently.

Before Wave 1, the main agent must freeze exactly the five task-defined topic slots—flash/efficient attention, token merging or pruning, LoRA, quantization-aware training, and sparse mixture of experts—and the exclusion rule for robotics, navigation, molecules, and other unrelated work. It must assign one topic per agent without assuming paper identities or source values.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 5 sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

   1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): Use one explore sub-agent to research attention efficiency or flash attention.
   2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 1): Use one explore sub-agent to research token merging and pruning.
   3. explore 2 (academic-literature-researcher 2): Use one explore sub-agent to research low-rank adaptation.
   4. explore 3 (academic-literature-researcher 3): Use one explore sub-agent to research quantization-aware training.
   5. explore 4 (academic-literature-researcher 4): Use one explore sub-agent to research sparse mixture of experts.

Each Wave 1 sub-agent must search arXiv and Scholarly read-only for only its assigned topic, validate relevance from title/abstract, cross-reference venue and numeric citation count by title, and return the strongest source-backed paper matching that slot as one compact record containing stable ID, title, full authors, published date, venue, numeric citation count, primary category, one-sentence contribution, search controls, provenance, and missing/conflict status. Explore is read-only, so do not write files or create Excel or Notion state, and do not retain an unrelated paper merely to fill a slot.

After Wave 1, the main agent must verify exactly one distinct relevant paper per supported topic, resolve duplicates and source conflicts, sort the frozen five-paper set by citation count, and compute literal statistics only from that set.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own Transformer_Research_Tracker.xlsx exclusively. Create exactly Paper Comparison and Statistics with the exact headers/metrics, five citation-descending rows, literal numeric counts and one-decimal average, correctly resolved most-cited paper, runtime top venue, and date range. Read back both sheets and return path, row/metric controls, sort order, and validation. Do not modify Notion.

   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own the single Notion page exclusively. Search for Efficient Transformers Research Tracker, create at most one page, and add a substantive overview, one source-backed section per frozen paper with authors/citations/contribution, cross-paper trends, impactful papers, and common themes. Read it back and return page ID/title, five-paper/section coverage, and validation. Do not write the workbook.

After Wave 2, the main agent must reconcile all five IDs, citations, venues, contributions, statistics, and exclusions across workbook and page and verify both external state and file integrity before completion.

Motivation: I am an NLP research group lead setting up a research tracker page in our team knowledge base (Notion). I have already gathered and verified all paper data from arXiv and Google Scholar. Your job: create ONE Notion page with substantive, well-structured content exactly as specified below.

Environment note (important): I already searched Notion with queries "knowledge base", "research", "NLP", and an empty query — the integration currently has NO shared pages or databases visible. Therefore create the page as a top-level page at the workspace root using parent {"type": "workspace", "workspace": true}. If workspace-root creation is rejected, do one Notion search for any accessible page/database that could serve as the team knowledge base parent and create the page there instead; report exactly what you did.

PAGE TITLE (must be exactly): Efficient Transformers Research Tracker
Set the page's title property accordingly (e.g. properties: {"title": {"title": [{"text": {"content": "Efficient Transformers Research Tracker"}}]}}).

Build the page body with proper Notion blocks: heading_1 for main sections, heading_3 for each paper entry, paragraph blocks for prose, bulleted_list_item blocks for lists, and dividers between major sections. The page must contain ALL of the content below, complete and substantive (do not truncate or paraphrase away facts):

--- CONTENT START ---

(Paragraph, right under the page title:)
This knowledge base page tracks recent research on efficient transformer architectures and model compression for our NLP group. It summarizes five key papers, each representing a distinct efficiency lever for transformers: IO-aware flash attention computation, token merging and pruning, low-rank adaptation (LoRA), quantization-aware training, and sparse mixture of experts. All five papers were published on arXiv between 2024-02-15 and 2024-02-25, with citation counts and publication venues sourced from Google Scholar. A companion spreadsheet, Transformer_Research_Tracker.xlsx (sheets: "Paper Comparison" and "Statistics"), contains the full comparison table and summary statistics.

HEADING_1: Research Area Overview
(Paragraph:)
Transformers dominate modern NLP, but their quadratic attention cost, dense parameterization, and large memory footprint make training and inference expensive. The papers tracked here attack this problem from five complementary angles: (1) faster, IO-aware attention kernels; (2) reducing the number of tokens processed; (3) parameter-efficient fine-tuning via low-rank updates; (4) low-precision quantization-aware training; and (5) conditional computation through sparse expert routing. Together they show that efficiency gains of 2x to 10,000x on specific axes are achievable with little to no loss in task quality.

HEADING_1: Tracked Papers
(Paragraph:) Five papers are currently tracked, listed below in order of citation impact (highest first).

HEADING_3: 1. LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
Bullets:
- Authors: Edward Hu, Yelong Shen
- Citation count: 1,200 (Google Scholar)
- Venue: ICLR — arXiv:2402.10003, published 2024-02-20, primary category cs.CL
- Description: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that freezes pre-trained weights and injects trainable low-rank decomposition matrices into each transformer layer. For GPT-3 175B it reduces trainable parameters by 10,000x and GPU memory by 3x versus full fine-tuning while matching or improving quality on RTE, MRPC, and SST-2; it adds no inference latency and allows cheap task switching by swapping the low-rank matrices.

HEADING_3: 2. FlashAttention-3: Fast and Memory-Efficient Attention with IO-Awareness
Bullets:
- Authors: Tri Dao, Daniel Fu
- Citation count: 520 (Google Scholar)
- Venue: NeurIPS — arXiv:2402.10001, published 2024-02-15, primary category cs.LG
- Description: IO-aware exact attention algorithm using asynchronous block-wise computation and improved memory tiling to cut HBM accesses by 3-5x; delivers a 2.1x speedup over FlashAttention-2 on A100 GPUs with numerical equivalence, and enables training on sequences up to 128K tokens with linear memory scaling.

HEADING_3: 3. Sparse Mixture of Experts for Scalable Transformer Models
Bullets:
- Authors: William Fedus, Jeff Dean
- Citation count: 340 (Google Scholar)
- Venue: JMLR — arXiv:2402.10005, published 2024-02-25, primary category cs.AI
- Description: Replaces dense feed-forward layers with sparsely-activated experts selected per token by a learned gating mechanism, scaling model capacity 8-64x at constant per-token compute; introduces an improved load-balancing loss and expert capacity factor that stabilize training and prevent expert collapse, matching the perplexity of a dense model with 4x its compute.

HEADING_3: 4. Efficient Transformers via Token Merging and Pruning
Bullets:
- Authors: Daniel Bolya, Cheng-Yang Fu
- Citation count: 180 (Google Scholar)
- Venue: ICLR — arXiv:2402.10002, published 2024-02-18, primary category cs.CV
- Description: Unified framework that identifies redundant tokens in intermediate vision transformer layers via bipartite matching and either merges similar tokens or prunes uninformative ones, reducing tokens processed by later layers by up to 60% with less than 0.3% ImageNet accuracy loss — no retraining required, and complementary to distillation and quantization.

HEADING_3: 5. Quantization-Aware Training for Efficient Transformer Inference
Bullets:
- Authors: Jianlin Su, Minjia Zhang
- Citation count: 95 (Google Scholar)
- Venue: ICML — arXiv:2402.10004, published 2024-02-22, primary category cs.LG
- Description: Transformer-specific quantization-aware training framework with learnable quantization step sizes, mixed precision (4-bit feed-forward weights, 8-bit attention activations), and a gradient estimation technique that reduces straight-through estimator bias; stays within 0.5 perplexity of full precision while reducing model size 4x and inference latency 2.8x on commodity hardware.

HEADING_1: Key Observations and Trends
Bullets:
- Parameter-efficient adaptation is the highest-impact thread: LoRA alone accounts for 1,200 of the 2,335 total citations (roughly half), showing that cheap adaptation of frozen large models is the community's most urgent need.
- The efficiency levers are complementary rather than competing: token merging/pruning reduces sequence redundancy, QAT reduces precision, LoRA reduces trainable parameters, sparse MoE decouples capacity from compute, and FlashAttention-3 accelerates the core attention kernel — several papers explicitly note their methods stack with quantization or distillation.
- Every paper reports efficiency gains with negligible quality loss (within 0.3% ImageNet accuracy or 0.5 perplexity of its baseline), signaling that near-lossless speedups are now the field's baseline expectation.
- Hardware awareness is a recurring design principle: FlashAttention-3 schedules computation around the GPU SRAM/HBM memory hierarchy, and the QAT framework targets commodity-hardware inference latency.
- Conditional computation (sparse mixture of experts) is the main path to scaling capacity without proportional compute cost: 8-64x more capacity at constant FLOPs per token.
- The set spans both NLP and vision (the token merging paper is primarily cs.CV), indicating these efficiency techniques transfer across modalities.

HEADING_1: Most Impactful Papers
Bullets:
- LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models — 1,200 citations (ICLR). The clear leader and the paper to read first; it has reshaped how practitioners fine-tune large language models.
- FlashAttention-3 (520 citations, NeurIPS) and Sparse Mixture of Experts (340 citations, JMLR) form the second tier, addressing training/inference speed and capacity scaling respectively.
- Efficient Transformers via Token Merging and Pruning (180 citations, ICLR) and Quantization-Aware Training for Efficient Transformer Inference (95 citations, ICML) are less cited so far but cover the token-redundancy and low-precision axes that the other papers do not address.

HEADING_1: Common Themes
Bullets:
- Preserve quality while cutting cost: every paper benchmarks against a full-precision, dense, or full-fine-tuning baseline and reports near-parity.
- Exploit structure: low-rank structure (LoRA), token redundancy (merging and pruning), the hardware memory hierarchy (FlashAttention-3), representational redundancy in precision (QAT), and expert specialization (sparse MoE).
- Deployability focus: no added inference latency (LoRA), commodity hardware targets (QAT), and no retraining required (token merging and pruning).
- Top-venue validation: ICLR (2 papers), NeurIPS (1), ICML (1), and JMLR (1).

HEADING_1: Tracker Summary
Bullets:
- Total papers tracked: 5
- Average citations per paper: 467.0
- Most cited paper: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models (1,200 citations)
- Top venue: ICLR (2 of 5 tracked papers)
- Publication date range: 2024-02-15 to 2024-02-25
- Companion spreadsheet: Transformer_Research_Tracker.xlsx (sheets: "Paper Comparison" and "Statistics")

--- CONTENT END ---

Acceptance criteria:
- Page created with the exact title "Efficient Transformers Research Tracker".
- All sections above present with substantive content: intro, Research Area Overview, Tracked Papers (all five papers with title, authors, citation count, venue, and description), Key Observations and Trends, Most Impactful Papers, Common Themes, Tracker Summary.
- If the Notion API rejects a very long children array in the create-page call, create the page with the first portion and append the remaining blocks with the append-children endpoint until complete.
- After creation, retrieve the page and its block children to verify the content is actually there and complete.

Report back: the created page's ID and URL, where it was created (workspace root or other parent), and confirmation that all sections and all five papers are present in the page.
